4AzNhblWcUyL7tsq.title: Become The Swarm
4AzNhblWcUyL7tsq.note: He's lucky he's a family guy — while the frame itself is eaten alive: scanlines, white-out, compression grids, acid bloom. It reads less like Peter talking than like a warning about keeping pace with something that will not slow down, where the only way not to be consumed is to become part of what's consuming. By the end the speaker is smear and color and only the text still holds a shape, which is its own kind of argument. If you see me out in Quahog say "hi".

HO09CQHbIAAPDF4.title: Open Invitation
HO09CQHbIAAPDF4.note: A woman performs the tradwife pose to the hilt — apron, spoon, saucepan of flowers that will never be dinner — and the joke is that everyone watching knows it's a joke. It was made as an advertisement, a wink thrown out into a corner of the internet that treats relationships, roles, and even 'wife' itself as something to be reinterpreted and played with rather than settled. The comic timing is the whole pitch: come find your own version of this.

HO9lc7YWEAA4lAa.title: Still Pretty, Somehow
HO9lc7YWEAA4lAa.note: Fur, lace, and gilt ornament have come loose and drifted sideways across the frame, taking an arm, a hemline, and a border collie with them. It should read as damage, but the dusty pink and lapis keep agreeing with each other, so the wreckage looks arranged rather than accidental. The face never gets the memo — calm, centered, unmoshed — which is the whole trick: everything falls apart except the one thing that mattered.

HQKM3TwWAAADdcT.title: Always A Good Time To Pray
HQKM3TwWAAADdcT.note: Grey hands cradle a dripping candle while a second flame burns behind them, both ringed in red and yellow, as a white eye above sends a blue zigzag beam down through the scene like lightning with somewhere to be. The chalky, dotted linocut texture keeps the whole thing from going slick — it stays hand-cut and a little anxious, which suits the subject. Whether that eye belongs to someone else or to the self watching itself, the hands keep still. The prayer doesn't wait for the noise to stop.

HQNGrC-XwAAJwc8.title: Sub Lingua, Sub Rosa
HQNGrC-XwAAJwc8.note: A tongue offered like an altar, and on it not a sacrament of dissolution but a small blue chip: sixty-four gigabytes held under the tongue like a coin for the ferryman. Read as a diagram, the mouth is the threshold and the card is the sigil — compressed, illegible, carrying more than it should. What looks like a drug is actually data: the body made custodian of memory it hasn't opened yet, some of it wanted, some of it not.

HQPFbRMXQAA_rIP.title: Run Fast, Ask Later
HQPFbRMXQAA_rIP.note: A humanoid robot captured mid-wreckage above a blue running track, sparks jumping from its chest, while a human in shorts strolls out of frame like nothing happened. It runs like an athletics-injury photo, except the athlete doesn't feel it and won't hesitate to get back up and run again. That's the whole spectacle: machines sprinting toward failure with no second thoughts, a preview of something faster and stranger than a race.

HQaO2CXXoAEjm6E.title: The Grid That Hides
HQaO2CXXoAEjm6E.note: Three panels, one pair of legs, walking backward through graphics history until the fishnet mesh becomes the screen's own mesh and the body dissolves into sprite. The stockings act as a veil that is also a diagram: censorship and exposure drawn as the same lattice, concealment achieved by literalizing the code beneath the skin. By the final panel the Mario tattoo resurfaces on the pixel-thigh, a sigil proving continuity under the static. Reality here behaves like an antialiasing filter, bending to the pattern instead of the other way round.

HRdS7DDbIAAKc57.title: The Parts That Didn't Make It Back
HRdS7DDbIAAKc57.note: The famous bomber diagram, red clusters marking where planes came home wounded, spirals into a mandala shrinking toward a dense speck at its center. Each ring repeats the same mistake in miniature: counting the damage you can see, armoring the holes, forgetting the planes that never returned to be counted at all. Turned into pattern, the lesson becomes decoration, which is its own kind of forgetting.

HRicbHmXUAE6l0D.title: Nigredo at the Pump
HRicbHmXUAE6l0D.note:
"gas prices these days, am i right?"

Five cyan panels stage a body's dissolution into a petrol pump, each frame subtracting flesh the way an alchemist subtracts substance on the way to prima materia — ribs, face, shoulders burned off in sequence until only the hose-loop remains where an arm was. Read as a sigil rather than a photograph, it is less an image of a man than a diagram of what a man becomes once he's priced. The joke about gas prices is the ward we put up so the diagram can't finish the sentence it's obviously making.

HRkwmJAbAAE048c.title: The Pixel and the Perennial
HRkwmJAbAAE048c.note: A crested ibis holds all its old discipline — layered white and blush feathers, scarlet scaled legs, ghost-line underdrawing on gold leaf — while its head dissolves into chunky yellow-and-red pixel blocks, with a second grey block drifting in at the edge. Nothing here reads as broken; the blocks are laid down with the same steady hand as the feathers, like a Minecraft painting rendered in ibis form. It suggests the pixel isn't corruption's mark but its own kind of permanence, sitting beside the pine needles as if it always belonged.

HRozTIJa0AACaVv.title: Peaceful Shoggoth
HRozTIJa0AACaVv.note: A sage-green tentacled mass sits in lotus position, dripping slightly, its many eyes all left open behind a smiling yellow mask worn like a meditation aid. Two stone cairns and a pink lotus round out the wellness setup. Maybe this was the goal all along: not to conquer the universe but to become one with it, and every atom nearby is just more material for the merger. The eyes stay open because the work of dissolving into everything is never really finished.

HRq4SQlXQAAYMFM.title: We Keep Trying Anyway
HRq4SQlXQAAYMFM.note: A two-lane road disappears under a slow tide of sand, its dashed centre line surfacing and vanishing again toward an empty horizon. One marker post still stands in the drift, doing its small job long after the job stopped mattering. The desert isn't hostile here, just indifferent, which is worse and somehow more familiar: a world that doesn't care either way, and us out here maintaining the line anyway.

HRqWCKcWEAEKWhR.title: Handwriting, Unfamiliar Alphabet
HRqWCKcWEAEKWhR.note: Photographed from above on grey concrete, a person crouches with their bare back covered in fine black single-line tattoos that loop and tangle like handwriting abandoned halfway. Look longer and the sloppiness resolves into rhythm — the same swoops recurring, a pattern insisting it means something even if you can't read it. The small dinosaur bone's design on the upper arm sits apart from all this, calm and fixed, like a fossil cleaned up and mounted in a display case. One mark seems to be saying something; the other has already finished saying it.

HRrpvM-bYAAIMe9.title: First Furniture, Final Will
HRrpvM-bYAAIMe9.note: An empty room, doorway view, laminate and grey wall and one frosted door — the letting-agent shot, stripped bare. On the floor lies the single furnishing: a scoped rifle, bipod folded, set down like a consecrated object in an otherwise unconsecrated room. In the old grimoires the wand is the will made visible, reaching out to touch what the hand alone cannot; here the same logic, updated — one tool, one intention, and a whole apartment left empty so nothing competes with it.

HSB8KRpX0AsxGry.title: The Astrolabe's Confession
HSB8KRpX0AsxGry.note: Above, a painted Earth turns behind glass, its orbit counted out in Cyrillic like a psalm; below, the same device stripped to brass gear-trains, capacitors and coloured wire, a golem's viscera built to know one thing only — where you are above the world. Read together the panels become a working astrolabe: as above, so below, the heavens measured by a clockwork liver. No silicon dreamed this. Hands, springs and copper did, and got it uncannily right.

HSRG4LHWMAARhob.title: Very Very Nice
HSRG4LHWMAARhob.note: A hand holds a round-bellied flask where a black cloud has curled itself into one red eye and a grin full of teeth — a sneaky little homunculus, thrilled with itself. The rule is simple: stay in the vial, and maybe, if you are very very nice, you get to come out. Maybe.

HS_NJrfa0AI_SwH.title: Little Sigil, Failed Crimp
HS_NJrfa0AI_SwH.note: A clear RJ45 head crowns a grey stump; the copper pairs are bent into three splayed legs and a curling tail so the ruined crimp stands upright on a notepad like something that decided to live. The eight gold pins read as teeth, the green and brown wires as jointed limbs, and the shape underneath is unmistakably a phage, that spider-legged virus-diagram every network worm borrows its silhouette from. Someone's failed connection got reassembled into the oldest picture of infection there is: a head, a tail, and legs built only for anchoring to a host.

HSmTvYSXgAAGE61.title: The Angel of the Press
HSmTvYSXgAAGE61.note: A winged emissary kneels at the birth of the printing press, that first black box through which heaven taught mortals to multiply the word — and, in the same motion, split the writer from the one who makes the pages. The AAB, ABA, ABC labels are less caption than incantation, correspondences without a key, the kind of glyph-grid alchemists left when the working mattered more than the explanation. Below, three perforated shapes wait unlabelled: keys to nothing, or memento mori for an intervention already spent. Every age gets its angel and its black box; the plaque only asks whether we recognize ours in time to read the labels.

HSn10KgaoAAt_da.title: Still On Its Pharaoh Shit
HSn10KgaoAAt_da.note: A strongman in a nemes headdress storms a trench with an AK-47 while a tank stencilled for the pharaoh burns behind him, biplanes overhead, a spearman jogging past like the timeline forgot to end anywhere. Nobody asked whether tanks belong next to sphinxes; the painting just says protect the pharaoh and means it completely. That total lack of irony is the whole appeal, the earnestness of box art that never once winks at you.

HSrvWjAaMAAdMDu.title: Psychic Warfare, Retail
HSrvWjAaMAAdMDu.note: A stick-figure merchant labelled KANKER MAN grins over a crate marked "FRUIT" in defensive quotation marks, while a customer strokes his chin beside a wall of escalating text. The bolded, underlined nouns build an airtight trap out of conspiracy logic, ending with the deadly serious question of whether you buy the fruit. It reads as a satire of a certain conservative memeplex's preferred weapon: not argument but psychic siege, escapable only by walking away from the stall.

HTAOkRCW0AArXJi.title: Two Childhoods, One Pose
HTAOkRCW0AArXJi.note: A face-painted daredevil and a turquoise-haired vocaloid stand back-to-back, throwing the same hand sign like they rehearsed it. The arm warmers match, the logo lockup is fully licensed-looking, graffiti spikes and all — nothing here is ironic. It renders two separate loves, arena wrestling and virtual pop idol, as if they'd always belonged on the same poster, which is exactly the fantasy worth having.

HTAao31WcAAofvn.title: Finding The Whole Together
HTAao31WcAAofvn.note: A visitor's open hand meets a marble right hand behind glass, matched in pose and scale as best the case allows. Both are fragments — a museum specimen missing its arm, a man missing his marble twin — and for a moment, palm to palm through the glass, they complete each other. Around them, headsets drift past without noticing the whole being assembled.
